sentences.sentence: NHS inform lists asthma attacks, pneumonia and heart failure among the likely causes of sudden breathlessness.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Less common sudden causes include a severe allergic reaction, a collapsed lung and a blood clot in the lung.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A collapsed lung, or pneumothorax, is a partial collapse caused by a small tear in the lung surface, and a pulmonary embolism is a blockage in one of the blood vessels in the lung.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Breathlessness that lasts a long time is commonly linked to obesity, being unfit, poorly controlled asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), anaemia, heart failure and heart rhythm problems.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: In heart failure, fluid builds up in the lungs and makes breathing harder.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A panic attack or anxiety can make a person breathe fast or deeply, which is called hyperventilating.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, in which the airways narrow and make extra sticky mucus, causing wheeze and cough.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Typical COPD symptoms include increasing breathlessness when active, a persistent cough with phlegm and frequent chest infections.

sentences.sentence: The NHS lists breathlessness as the most common symptom of heart failure; it may happen after activity or at rest, may be worse when lying down, and may wake a person at night.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: It lists tiredness, swollen ankles and legs, and feeling lightheaded or fainting as other heart failure symptoms.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS trust leaflet says the most common symptom of a pulmonary embolism is breathlessness, with other symptoms including chest pain that is worse on breathing or coughing, cough, fever and coughing up blood.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says to call 999 or go to A&E for severe difficulty breathing, such as being unable to speak without pausing for breath.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Chest tightness, or pain that spreads to the arms, back, neck or jaw, is also a reason to call 999.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A GP practice page adds sudden confusion, or lips or skin turning pale, blue or grey, to the signs that need an emergency response.
sentences.note: Summary attributed to Conwy Medical Centre page.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises that a person should not drive themselves to A&E but should ask someone to take them or call an ambulance.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises contacting NHS 111 or the GP urgently for worsening breathlessness, feeling sick, coughing up blood, or pain or swelling in one leg.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says breathlessness that starts suddenly should be seen urgently by a GP because it may point to a problem with the airways or heart.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For breathlessness that comes on slowly, NHS inform advises seeing a GP if it has lasted more than a month, gets worse with activity or lying down, or comes with swollen ankles.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A GP will usually ask when the breathlessness started, what brings it on and whether lying down makes it worse.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: An NHS England pathway for persistent breathlessness lists blood tests, an ECG, a chest X-ray and spirometry among the first tests.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Spirometry is a breathing test that measures how much air a person can blow out and how fast.
sentences.note: Plain textbook definition.

sentences.sentence: If the cause is still unclear, the same pathway lists further tests such as a CT scan of the chest, an echocardiogram and ambulatory ECG monitoring.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Treatment depends on the cause.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: For COPD, treatment usually involves relieving symptoms with medicines such as inhalers, and pulmonary rehabilitation may help.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: Heart failure is managed with lifestyle changes and medicines or surgery.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: A blood clot in the lung can be treated with anticoagulants, which are drugs that thin the blood.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages).

sentences.sentence: One NHS leaflet describes relaxed breathing and pursed-lip breathing as techniques that can help a person regain control of their breathing.
